task.description: REVIEWER (WF-02 Step 2d) hard gate on REQ-159, run e153fd5.

result.notes:
1) Idiom/design-fidelity: both flagged deviations are well-justified, forced adaptations, not shortcuts. run_stub/4->5: design Sec 7.3 assumed the arity-1 install/2 wrapper shape could stay unchanged, but tv-labs/lua's Lua.encode!/2 requires the call's own Lua.t() to build a dynamic table, which only the documented arity-2 Lua.set!/3 callback form (fn args, lua -> end) exposes -- confirmed directly against deps/lua/lib/lua.ex, and every structural invariant the design actually cared about (one fold, one Lua.set!/3 call site per row, both capabilities and execution_context closed over once) is preserved. log's Lua.decode!/2 fix corrects an incorrect design assumption (Sec 6.1 step 1, that table args arrive pre-decoded) confirmed false against deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/value.ex -- without the explicit decode!, do_log would have leaked a raw {:tref, id} VM-internal reference into Logger metadata, which is a real bug the design's assumption would have caused. Recommendation: a small non-mandatory addendum to req159-lua-host-api-read.md is worth adding (same posture as REQ-156's non-blocking recommended addendum to REQ-149's design, req156-lua-memory-limit-impl.md Sec 6/OQ-3) documenting run_stub/5's real arity and the explicit Lua.decode!/2 step, so a future reader of the design doesn't re-derive this from platform.ex's moduledoc alone. This is NOT a gating requirement -- platform.ex's own moduledoc already documents both deviations thoroughly and correctly, which is sufficient to pass this gate; the addendum is documentation hygiene, not a correction of behavior.

2) Scope creep: confirmed none. Diff to @capability_matrix touches only the `stub` field of read_variable/get_instance_state/log rows (:not_yet_implemented -> :read_variable/:get_instance_state/:log); the `required` field for all 8 rows and the full rows for call_service/write_variable/emit_event/now/fail are byte-for-byte unchanged (verified against the diff hunk directly, not merely trusting ELIXIR-DEV's self-report). No new Lua.set!/3 call site introduced (INV-CAP-1 intact); still exactly 8 rows (INV-CAP-2 intact).

3) Decision-record consistency: consistent with decision 0014(e) -- every Repo.get/3 call site in this diff (exactly one, in fetch_instance_state/3) uses execution_context.prefix only, never anything derived from the script-supplied instance_id argument; the self-instance-only check happens strictly before any Repo call for a non-matching id. Consistent with REQ-150 Sec 3's naming and identity rule. Consistent with REQ-157's capability matrix -- required_capability values and Capabilities.check!/3 ordering (gate first, body second) both untouched.

4) Test quality: good. The sibling-vs-nonexistent indistinguishability test (platform_test.exs) is well-named, asserts both individual outcomes AND the equality of the two result tuples, which is the actual security property (not just 'both say forbidden' but 'identical response shape'), reducing flake risk since it doesn't depend on ordering or timing. Capability-denial tests exist for all 3 functions, asserting both the raised exception's :function and :capability_required fields distinctly, in line with REQ-157's existing pattern -- not flaky (no sleeps, no async races; async: false preserved for Sandbox global-state reasons, consistent with the existing file's own docstring rationale). Real-Postgres fixtures mirror the established event_store_test.exs idiom rather than inventing a new one.

5) LuaNumberMarshalling: to_lua/1 and from_lua/1 are both literally `def f(value), do: value` -- pure identity for every term(), including integer/float/nil per REQ-150 Sec 3, and pass-through (still identity, since the function has no branches) for every other shape (string/boolean/map/list), matching REQ-150's explicit scope note that non-numeric shapes get no invented behavior. No branching, no coercion logic exists to diverge from the rule. Confirmed exercised by a genuine round-trip test (read_variable with math.type() assertions on both an integer and a float) rather than merely referenced.

No blockers. No rework required. No anti-patterns.md entries triggered.
recommendations: Non-blocking: add a short addendum to lib/letflow/design/req159-lua-host-api-read.md documenting run_stub/5's real arity and the explicit Lua.decode!/2 step for log's context argument, mirroring the non-mandatory addendum precedent set by req156-lua-memory-limit-impl.md Sec 6/OQ-3 for req149-lua-memory-limit.md. Left to whoever next touches either document; not a precondition for TEST-DESIGNER to proceed.
